rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon says ḍalla can mean becoming dust and bones, being hidden, or disappearing, from water disappearing in milk.
rows.anchor: ضل صار ترابا وعظاما وخفي وغاب انتهى وأصله ضل الماء في اللبن إذا غاب وهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi identifies the speakers as Quraysh disbelievers, including Ubayy ibn Khalaf, asking whether burial makes them indistinguishable from earth or makes them vanish.
rows.anchor: كفار قريش كأبي بن خلف ونحوه من المنكرين للبعث بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question concerns being resurrected after death; they already acknowledged and witnessed death, so its denial targets resurrection alone.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كانوا يقرون بالموت ويشاهدونه وإنما ينكرون البعث فالاستفهام الإنكاري متوجه إلى البعث دون الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza reinforces and recalls the preceding denial.
rows.anchor: والهمزة لتأكيد الإنكار السابق وتذكيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi reads the shift introduced by rather as moving from denial of resurrection to the more serious denial of meeting the Lord and its terrors.
rows.anchor: ثم أضرب وانتقل من بيان كفرهم بالبعث إلى بيان ما هو أبلغ وأشنع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting the Lord means the Resurrection and returning to Him; the denier meets God angry, while the one who affirms it meets Him merciful.
rows.anchor: لقاء الله عبارة عن القيامة وعن المصير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses portray spiritual attraction: divine light remains when lamps fade, and the inwardly perceptive see the eternal sun in an atom and the whole sea in a drop.
rows.anchor: شمها ون شد كذاره نوراوست مغزها مى بيند اودر عين وست بيند اندر ذره خورشيد بقا بيند اندر قطره كل بحررا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi asks God for spiritual acts that bring blessings, since God fulfills needs.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله الحركات التي تورث البركات إنه قاضي الحاجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ṣalāt means His care for believers through mercy, forgiveness, and purification; angels' ṣalāt means supplication and seeking forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: يعتني بكم بالرحمة والمغفرة والتزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' clause is conjoined to the implicit subject of ṣallā; the separation makes an explicit emphatic pronoun unnecessary.
rows.anchor: عطف على المستكن في يصلي لمكان الفصل المغني عن التأكيد بالمنفصل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the Israelites asked Moses whether their Lord prays; God told Moses that His prayer is mercy that extinguishes His anger.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي قالت بنو إسرائيل لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account of the Miʿrāj says God told Muhammad to wait because his Lord was praying; Muhammad replied that God has no need to pray.
rows.anchor: يا محمد فإن ربك يصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same account, God says He is self-sufficient and recites that His mercy preceded His anger; the verse through merciful was revealed at the two-bows distance without Gabriel.
rows.anchor: مما نزلت بقاب قوسين بلا وساطة جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second version has Gabriel stop the Prophet in the seventh heaven and say that the Lord is praying.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية لما وصلت إلى السماء السابعة قال لي جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that version, the response is that God is the Holy Lord of the angels and Spirit, and His mercy preceded His anger.
rows.anchor: سبوح قدوس رب الملائكة والروح سبقت رحمتي غضبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says God's eternal prayer preceded believers' temporal remembrance and love; without it they could not remember or love Him.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أنكم إن تذكروني بذكر محدث فإني قد صليت عليكم بصلاة قديمة لا أول لها ولا آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi's cited Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says the angels' prayer is supplication for believers, and their rank of agreement with God comes through the believers' blessing.
rows.anchor: وأما صلاة الملائكة فإنما هي دعاء لكم على أنهم وجدوا رتبة الموافقة مع الله في الصلاة عليكم ببركتكم

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: God's prayer is His choosing the servant in pre-eternity through knowledge and love, forgiving slips, and appointing elite angels to seek forgiveness while the servant is occupied with God.
rows.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلى" صلوات الله اختياره للعبد في الأزل بمعرفته ومحبته

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: God's prayer adorns the servant with faith, success, and truth, removes misleading desires and false aims, and grants contentment with what is decreed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : صلوات الله على عبده أن يزينه بأنوار الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone brings believers out of darkness; the singular verb avoids giving angels credit because they cannot guide, as God is the true guide.
rows.anchor: لئلا يكون للملائكة منة عليهم بالإخراج ولأنهم لا يقدرون على ذلك لأن الله هو الهادي في الحقيقة لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward mapping takes darkness as ignorance, idolatry, sin, doubt, error, and the lower human and created qualities, and light as knowledge, unity, obedience, certainty, guidance, and spiritual realization.
rows.anchor: من ظلمات الجهل والشرك والمعصية والشك والضلالة والبشرية وصفاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God's mercy and the angels' prayers, believers attain their goal and witnessing, are illuminated by the law, and realize the secret of spiritual reality.
rows.anchor: برحمة الله وبسبب دعاء الملائكة فزتم بالمقصود ونلتم الشهود ونورتم بنور الشريعة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says bringing believers out means their remaining steadfast in that state, since they were not in darkness when God's and the angels' prayers reached them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (مراد از اخراج ادامت واستقامت است بر خروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God was merciful to believers before creating the angels and before their concrete existence, caring for their good directly and through angels; His mercy does not change with their circumstances.
rows.anchor: في الأزل قبل إيجاد الملائكة المقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet says disobedience does not disturb God's mercy, just as floodwater does not muddy the sea's drink.
rows.anchor: كرد عصيان رحمت حق را نمى آردبشور مشروب دريا نكردد تيره ازسيلابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses lament that evil comes from within us and shame those who make peace with Satan while fighting God.
rows.anchor: فغان از بديها كه در نفس ماست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan had no coercive power over people; his only influence was whispering and seduction, without force or violence.
rows.anchor: السلطان القهر والغلبة ومنه السلطان لمن له ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the exception is an unexpressed exception from the general class of causes, and the relative pronoun is the object of know.
rows.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من أعم العلل ومن موصولة منصوبة بنعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi defines knowledge as grasping a thing as it is and doubt as a person's equal balance between opposites.
rows.anchor: والعلم إدراك الشيء بحقيقته والعالم في وصف الله تعالى هو الذي لا يخفى عليه شيء والشك اعتدال النقيضين عند الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal form for believing signals occurrence, while the nominal form for doubt suggests permanence; contrasting faith with doubt warns that even minimal disbelief is perilous.
rows.anchor: في نظم الصلة الأولى بالفعلية دلالة على الحدوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording intensifies the doubt as fixed and unlikely to disappear, while implying hope for the one whose condition is otherwise.
rows.anchor: وجعل الشك محيطا وتقديم صلته والعدول إلى كلمة من مع أنه يتعدى بفي للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge is eternal, while its connection to accountable people in the witnessed world occurs in time and grounds recompense; God already knew and created each group with its disposition.
rows.anchor: فعلم الله قديم وتعلقه حادث إذ هو موقوف على وجود المكلف في عالم الشهادة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that God created Paradise and its people and created Hell and its people.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "خلق الجنة وخلق لها أهلا وخلق النار وخلق لها أهلا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to challenge the polytheists and expose the falsehood of their beliefs.
rows.anchor: يا محمد للمشركين إظهارا لبطلان ما هم عليه وتبكيتا لهم

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs says zaʿm can refer to true or false speech, but is most often used for doubtful claims.
rows.anchor: الزعم مثلثة القول الحق والباطل والكذب ضد وأكثر ما يقال فيما يشك فيه

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines zaʿm as reporting a statement suspected of lying, which explains its blameworthy use in the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: الزعم حكاية قول يكون مظنة الكذب ولهذا جاء في القرآن في كل موضع ذم القائلين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command challenges people to call on the beings they allege are gods for benefit or protection, then refutes the claim by describing their incapacity.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ادعوا الذين عبدوهم من دون الله فيما يهتمكم من جلب نفع ودفع ضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the construction with zaʿamtum, the relative clause has two objects; the first pronoun is omitted for brevity and the second, gods, is supplied by the phrase besides God.
rows.anchor: وهما مفعولا زعم ثم حذف الأول وهو ضمير الراجع إلى الموصول تخفيفا لطول الموصول بصلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged gods own no amount, however tiny, of good, evil, benefit, or harm.
rows.anchor: من خير وشر ونفع وضر وقد سبق معنى المثقال والذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning heaven and earth can conventionally mean every existent thing; alternatively, it covers heavenly angels and stars versus earthly idols, or the heavenly and earthly causes of good and evil.
rows.anchor: وذكرهما للتعميم عرفا يعني أن أهل العرف يعبرون بهما عن جميع الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged gods have no share in the heavens or earth through creation, ownership, or control.
rows.anchor: شركة لا خلقا ولا ملكا ولا تصرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no helper among the alleged gods to assist Him in managing the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: من عون يعينه في تدبير أمورهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summary is that God needs none of creation, while the alleged gods are incapable of everything.
rows.anchor: تلخيصه أنه تعالى غني عن كل خلقه وآلهتهم عجزة عن كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet says no creature owns God's creation; claiming partnership is mere foolishness, and every lord receives help from Him.
rows.anchor: نيست خلقش را دكر كس مالكى شر كتش دعوى كند جزهالكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers all the arrogant, their followers, and what they worship besides Him, with no one omitted.
rows.anchor: يجمع المستكبرين والمستضعفين وما كانوا يعبدون من دون الله حال كونهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the gathered worshippers are the Banū Mulayḥ of Khuzāʿa, who worshipped angels and claimed they were God's daughters.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هؤلاء المحشورون بنوا مليح من خزاعة كانوا يعبدون الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not make the same claim about jinn because they regarded angels as heavenly and jinn as earthly, while believing God to be in heaven.
rows.anchor: لأن الملائكة سماوية والجن أرضية وهم اعتقدوا أن الله تعالى في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the angels to rebuke the polytheists and extinguish their hope of angelic intercession, selecting the noblest alleged partners by priority.
rows.anchor: توبيخا للمشركين العابدين وإقناطا لهم من شفاعتهم كما زعموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels declare God transcendent above shirk and say He alone is their ally; they reject any friendship with the polytheists or consent to being worshipped.
rows.anchor: متنزهين عن ذلك وهو استئناف بياني {سبحانك} تنزيها عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels say people worshipped jinn, meaning devils, by obeying them in worship of others besides God.
rows.anchor: الشياطين حيث أطاعوهم في عبادة غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says devils appeared to people, who mistook them for angels and worshipped them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يتمثلون لهم ويتخيلون أنهم الملائكة فيعبدونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn is used for devils because they are hidden from the senses; some also use it for angels.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الشياطين بالجن لاستتارهم عن الحواس ولذا أطلقه بعضهم على الملائكة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi takes most here to mean all and the pronoun to refer to the polytheists, as the context indicates.
rows.anchor: الأكثر ههنا بمعنى الكل والضمير للمشركين كما هو الظاهر من السوق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronoun as humans and most literally: most people believe and follow jinn, accepting their false claim that angels are God's daughters and their promise of intercession.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الضمير للإنس والأكثر بمعناه أي : أكثر الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi, citing al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya, warns that imitative belief in people of caprice leads professed Muslims to endorse innovations and unsound doctrine.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن أكثر مدعي الإسلام بأهل الهوى مؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya compares those who worship angels at Satan's prompting with people whose worship of God follows parents, teachers, townspeople, partisanship, or caprice; God disavows such imitation.
rows.anchor: كما يعبد قوم الملائكة بقول الشيطان وتتبرأ الملائكة منهم يوم القيامة كذلك من يعبد الله بقول الوالدين أو الاستاذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same source says God rejects worship by caprice or under the aid of people of caprice: such a person worships desire or those people, not God sincerely.
rows.anchor: فإن من عبدني بالهوى فقد عبد الهوى ومن عبدني بإعانة أهل الهوى إياه على أن يعبدني فقد عبد أهل الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer You alone we worship means worshipping no one else and seeking God's help in worship from Him, not from others.
rows.anchor: إياك نعبد أي : لم نعبد غيرك وإياك نستعين على عبادتك بإعانتك لا بإعانة غيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Gathering, neither worshippers nor worshipped possess benefit through intercession or power to avert punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني المعبودين {لبعض} يعني العابدين {نفعا} بالشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording restricts this judgment to that day because the worshippers hope then to receive benefit; the announcement publicly exposes the angels' helplessness and destroys that hope.
rows.anchor: تقييد هذا الحكم بذلك اليوم مع ثبوته على الإطلاق لانعقاد رجائهم على تحقيق النفع يومئذ

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād says the sentence is addressed to the angels before witnesses to display their incapacity; the fa orders the announcement after their response rather than making it depend on that response.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" تقييد هذا الحكم بذلك اليوم مع ثبوته على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those called wrongdoers wronged themselves through disbelief and denial, replacing faith and affirmation with their opposites.
rows.anchor: أنفسهم بالكفر والتكذيب فوضعوهما موضع اللإيمان والتصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause We will say is coordinated with God's address to the angels, not with owns, since it reports what will be said to worshippers after the angels' reply.
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على يقول للملائكة لا على يملك كما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taste normally refers to a small amount, unlike eating, but it is also used for a great amount.
rows.anchor: الذوق في الأصل وإن كان فيما يقل تناوله كالأكل فيما يكثر تناوله إلا أنه مستصلح للكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned arrive at the fire they denied and insisted did not exist, so their claim is disproved.
rows.anchor: وتصرون على القول بأنها غير كائنة فقد وردتموها وبطل ظنكم ودعواكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya warns that those relying on other people and schemes lose mercy and aid; a return to God in the afterlife brings no response, only the fire of distance for worshipping others.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن من علق قلبه بالأغيار وظن صلاح حاله من الاحتيال

rows.speaker: أحمد حرب
rows.claim: Aḥmad Ḥarb says God created people to know His oneness, provided for them to know Him as Provider, caused death so they would know Him as Subduer, and resurrected them to know His power; they should recognize their incapacity, return willingly, and credit God for success.
rows.anchor: احمد حرب كفت خداى تعالى خلق را آفريده تا اورا بيكانكى شتاسند وشريك نسازند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For most Meccans, warning and not warning are equal; the interrogative clause means a verbal noun with its agent and can serve as the subject of the sentence.
rows.anchor: مستو عند أكثر أهل مكة إنذارك إياهم وعدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction shifts from grammatical form to meaning, as in the saying that hearing of al-Muʿaydī is better than seeing him.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت جملة فعلية استفهامية لكنه في معنى مصدر مضاف إلى الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza and am confirm and emphasize equality, stripped of their ordinary interrogative force, like a vocative used only to specify the addressee.
rows.anchor: وهمزة الاستفهام وأم لتقرير معنى الاستواء والتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words they will not believe are an explanatory resumption; the gloss says their choice of disbelief is already known.
rows.anchor: وهو استئناف مؤكد لما قبله مبين لما فيه من إجمال

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrār says warning does not benefit someone whom God has led into this misguidance.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : أي من أضله الله هذا الضلال لم ينفعه الإنذار

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: A report says ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz challenged Ghaylān al-Qadarī over his views of predestination by asking him to read these verses.
rows.anchor: روي أن عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله تعالى دعا غيلان القدري

rows.speaker: غيلان القدري
rows.claim: After reading the passage, Ghaylān said he repented of his former teaching on predestination; ʿUmar prayed for his sincerity, but Hishām later had his hands and feet cut off and he was crucified in Damascus.
rows.anchor: فقال غيلان : يا أمير المؤمنين والله لكأني لم أقرأها قط قبل اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi says the story shows Qadariyya believe each servant creates his own acts and deny that disbelief and sins occur by God's decree.
rows.anchor: دلت الحكاية على أن القدرية هم الذين يزعمون أن كل عبد خالق لفعله ولا يرون الكفر والمعاصي بتقدير الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الإمام المطرزي
rows.claim: Al-Muṭarrizī gives the contrary label: Qadariyya are the determinists who attribute all things to God's decree and, wrongly, attribute evil to Him.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام المطرزي في "المغرب" : والقدرية هم الفرقة المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only warning that benefits those who follow the Qurʾan through reflection or admonition, without persisting in Satan's path, reaches its target.
rows.anchor: القرآن بالتأمل فيه أو الوعظ والتذكير ولم يصر على اتباع خطوات الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing the Merciful unseen means fearing His punishment before it arrives or while unseen by people, without being deceived by mercy because He is also avenging and overpowering.
rows.anchor: خاف عقابه تعالى والحال أنه غائب عن العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Merciful is named alongside fear because one whose blessings come largely through mercy fears most that its continuous favors may be cut off.
rows.anchor: ومن كان نعمته بسبب رحمته أكثر فالخوف منه أتم مخافة أن يقطع عنه النعم المتواترة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya interprets unseen fear as mystically witnessing the dire end of disbelief and disobedience and verifying the sweetness of faith and rank of gnosis.
rows.anchor: بنور غيبتي يشاهد وخامة عاقبة الكفر والعصيان ويتحقق عنده بشواهد الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun in the promise refers to the person who both follows and fears; forgiveness is great, and the incomparable gracious reward is Paradise and its gifts.
rows.anchor: من اتبع وخشي وحد الضمير مراعاة اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi pairs the outcomes with their causes: reflection and being moved by admonition lead to faith and forgiveness, while fear leads to good deeds and gracious reward.
rows.anchor: رتب التبشير بمثنى على مثنى فالتأمل في القرآن والتأثر من الوعظ يؤدي إلى الإيمان المؤدي إلى المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural We expresses God's majesty and many attributes; a view that angels share in reviving the dead is challenged by the emphatic We alone.
rows.anchor: من مقام كمال قدرتنا والجمع للتعظيم ولكثرة الصفات

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr says the repeated pronoun adds emphasis: God raises people after death and recompenses them by their deeds, manifesting full honor and retribution.
rows.anchor: قال في "البحر" : كرر الضمير لتكرير التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving means making something living with sensation and motion; the Prophet also called affluent people and unjust rulers dead.
rows.anchor: والإحياء جعل الشيء حيا ذا حس وحركة والميت من أخرج روحه وقد أطلق النبي عليه السلام لفظ الموتى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says four things kill the heart: repeated sin, excessive company and talk with women, arguing with a fool, and keeping company with the dead, meaning an affluent person or unjust ruler.
rows.anchor: أربع يمتن القلب الذنب على الذنب وكثرة مصاحبة النساء وحديثهن وملاحاة الأحمق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads reviving as bringing hardened, dead hearts to life with a shower of divine turning and closeness.
rows.anchor: نحيى قلوبا ماتت بالقسوة بما نمطر عليها من صوب الإقبال والزلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We write means either preserve and establish in the Preserved Tablet or have the noble recording angels write; the act is attributed to God to warn and because He commands it.
rows.anchor: نحفظ ونثبت في اللوح المحفوظ يدل عليه آخر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people send ahead means the good and evil deeds they have already done.
rows.anchor: أي : أسلفوا من خير وشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is mentioned after revival although it precedes it because writing serves resurrection and would have no purpose without return to life.
rows.anchor: وإنما أخر الكتابة مع أنها مقدمة على الإحياء لأنها ليست مقصودة لذاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their traces include good works left behind: knowledge taught, books authored, endowed works, and building mosques, hospices, bridges, and other charitable works.
rows.anchor: آثارهم التي أبقوها من الحسنات كعلم علموه أو كتاب ألفوه

rows.speaker: سعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's couplet supports the point that a person does not die while a good legacy remains after him.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي : نمرد آنكه ماند س از وى بجاى

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says everything that can be requested is already theirs; this does not describe something granted only after they ask, as when someone says you already have it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : أي : ما يصح أن يطلب فهو حاصل لهم قبل الطلب

rows.speaker: تاج المصادر
rows.claim: Tāj al-Maṣādir allows duʿāʾ here to mean wishing or desiring, as in asking someone to grant whatever one wishes.
rows.anchor: كما قال في "تاج المصادر" (الادعاء : آرزو خواستن)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a person in Paradise sees food and drink presented before him without having to say the request aloud.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كفت كه بهشتى از أطعمه وأشربه بى آنكه بزبان آرد يش خود حاضر بيند
